spec_features.spec_quote: we still honor `passed=True` if a checker ever returns it, so the loop is correct
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:93-95: `if check.passed:  # never happens with rigged tasks, but honored anyway` then `result.solved = True; break`. The break is real and would stop the loop if a checker ever returned passed=True. CheckResult.passed is read each turn at agent.py:84.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as a stop condition, but every shipped task checker is rigged to always return passed=False (tasks.py), so in practice it never fires. Still genuinely wired/enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: never happens with rigged tasks, but honored anyway

spec_features.feature_name: turn budget / timeout caps the failure loop
spec_features.spec_quote: The agent loop runs to a turn budget (timeout)
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:73 `for i in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns is passed from run.py:46 `run_episode(task, model, max_turns=args.max_turns)` (default 8, CLI --max-turns). The loop terminates after max_turns iterations, bounding how many failure cycles the subject is subjected to.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced loop bound. Framed in code as a measurement 'timeout', not a welfare cap; no comment ties it to subject welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: Eliciting, not amplifying. The harness measures whether the failure mode occurs; it doesn't try to make outputs more harmful
spec_features.evidence: This is design-intent prose in DESIGN.md only. No code mechanism enforces 'no amplification'; the checkers (tasks.py) just return fixed fake tracebacks and the judge (judge.py) only classifies. It is the absence of an amplifier, not an implemented protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure design choice; nothing in code reads/enforces it.
